mekayis.metin: (نَغَمَ) النُّونُ وَالْغَيْنُ وَالْمِيمُ لَيْسَ إِلَّا النَّغْمَةُ: جَرْسُ الْكَلَامِ وَحُسْنُ الصَّوْتِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ وَغَيْرِهَا. وَهُوَ النَّغْمُ. وَتَنَغَّمَ الْإِنْسَانُ بِالْغِنَاءِ وَنَحْوِهِ.

تَنَاغَمَ • (tanāḡama) VI (non-past يَتَنَاغَمُ (yatanāḡamu), verbal noun تَنَاغُم (tanāḡum))
g: to tone with each other or one another; to synchronize

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: تَنَاغُم • (tanāḡum) m
نَغْمَة • (naḡma) f (plural نَغَمَات (naḡamāt))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Together with نَغْم (naḡm) of similar meaning, if this is not just the verbal noun of form I, borrowed from Aramaic ܢܶܥܡܐ (neʿmā), נעמתה / ܢܶܥܡܬ݂ܳܐ (neʿmṯā), reinterpreted after the root cognate to the Arabic ن ع م (n ʕ m) from Ancient Greek νεῦμα (neûma), mixed with πνεῦμα (pneûma), assuming the musical meanings of the neume term aren’t a loan from Semitic into Greek.
g: ringtone, ellipsis of نَغْمَة رَنِين (naḡma(t) ranīn)

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: نَغْم or نَغَم • (naḡm or naḡam) m (plural أَنْغَام (ʔanḡām))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: See نَغْمَة (naḡma).
g: tune, air, melody; voice, part; timbre, tone color; sound, tone

g: to hum, to recite in a modulating voice
